subject: Hosted API counting rules for split streaming outputs and discount banding

Subject: Hosted API: counting for streaming + tool outputs

Camila —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing streaming chat experience and we have a couple of nitty-gritty billing questions before we go to procurement:

1) If we do partial streaming (client displays tokens as they arrive) and the model emits a long reply in multiple chunks, how is rounding applied — per-chunk, per-request, or per-session?

2) We use a system prompt (150 tokens) + user prompt (230 tokens) and the model calls an internal tool that returns a 320-token structured payload which the model then integrates into the response (150 tokens). Which parts count as "input" vs "output" for metering? Is the tool payload billed as output or as a separate tool charge?

3) Assume we hit a discount threshold mid-month (e.g., crossing from 100k to 250k tokens). Does per-request rounding push you into a higher band earlier? How is rounding handled when computing band thresholds?

We want to prepare an SOW but need sample invoice-able examples to show to our finance team. Can you share a short worked example for the above scenarios and the current hosted rate card (incl. discount bands)?

Appreciate quick guidance — our procurement call is Thurs.

—Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. I looped in engineering and billing; below are concise, practical answers and a worked example attached (storlytics-sample-counting.xlsx). TL;DR: we meter per-request but aggregate monthly for discounts; rounding is applied at the per-request level before monthly aggregation. Details follow.

Metering rules (hosted API, standard):
- Base model metering = input tokens (system + user + tool inputs) + output tokens (model generations).
- Tool outputs (responses produced by an external tool and injected back into the model) are billed as output tokens if they are generated by a Redwood-enabled tool or returned by an integrated third-party tool in the response path. Practically: if your tool returns 320 tokens and we include them in the response payload, those tokens count as output.
- Streaming chunk rounding: we round token counts per request, not per chunk. For streaming responses the full request's tokens are tallied once the request completes; we do not charge per chunk. If a long-running request times out mid-stream, we bill what was emitted and rounded for that request at that moment.
- Rounding convention: we round to the nearest whole token (token counts are integers). If your client fragments bytes into multiple network frames, that does not affect token accounting.
- Discount bands: discounts are computed on monthly aggregated token usage after per-request rounding. That means many small requests that round up can increase your monthly totals vs unrounded raw token decimals, but band thresholds are evaluated on the post-rounding monthly sum.

Worked example (see spreadsheet for line-by-line):
Scenario: 1 request that uses system=150, user=230, tool-return=320, model-final-output=150.
- Inputs = system (150) + user (230) = 380 input tokens.
- Tool is invoked; tool returns 320 tokens which are inserted into the response path. Billing: tool-return = 320 output tokens.
- Model generation after tool = 150 output tokens.
- Total billed for the request = input 380 + output (320 + 150) = 850 tokens.
- We round per-request to integers (already integers here). If the model were to stream in 3 frames of 50 tokens each for the final output, you'd still be billed for the full 150 output tokens once the request completes.

Edge-case: partial-complete requests
- If a streaming session is aborted by the client mid-generation and you've received 60 of the intended 150 output tokens, we bill only the emitted tokens (plus inputs/tool costs) for that request: e.g., input 380 + output 320 (tool) + output 60 = 760 tokens for that aborted request. That 760 is rounded per-request and contributes to the monthly total.

Discount interaction example:
- Suppose your monthly usage pre-discount is 99,900 tokens (just below a 100k band). If you have 200 requests that each round up adding 1 token (200 tokens) the post-rounding monthly sum would be 100,100 which crosses the 100k band. Discount for the next band would apply to the portion of usage in that band in our billing model. We compute discounts on tiered usage (not retroactive for prior tiers).

Camila — very helpful, thank you. A couple follow-ups after reviewing the spreadsheet: 

1) For our compliance report, can you confirm whether the tool-return tokens are labeled separately on the invoice lines? We need to show"tool-generated" vs "model-generated" counts to our auditors.

2) Our engineering team uses optimistic client-side aggregation (they buffer several short streaming requests and send a single combine request to the model). In that combined-request case are inputs still counted as sent in that single request (we assume yes), and if the combine-request fails partially we want to understand how partiality is recorded (per request basis, as you described).

3) Pricing: can you outline how discounts are applied at invoice time for a mixed-month where 70% of tokens are from tool outputs? Do tool outputs count toward the same monthly usage bucket?

If all that checks out we'll ask procurement to proceed; please send the formal quote & SOW with the deal id so we can raise a PO.

Alex/Priya — quick answers and next steps: 

1) Invoice labeling: yes — the hosted invoice can include line items broken out by "model-input", "model-output", and "tool-output" counts. We'll include the raw counts used for discount computation so your auditors can reconcile.

2) Client-side aggregation: counted as a single request when you submit the combined payload. Partial failures are billed on a per-request basis as described earlier (only emitted tokens for aborted requests).

3) Discounts & tool outputs: tool-output tokens are included in your same monthly aggregation and contribute to tiered discounts. The invoice will show the tiered calculation: usage buckets, effective discount per bucket, and the billed amount.

Next steps: I have asked finance to prepare a formal quote and SOW referencing deal RDW-4591. Attached is the standard hosted rate card and a workbook with the worked examples. If you confirm the scope (monthly commit estimate in the spreadsheet) we can produce a committed discount quote or proceed on pay-as-you-go.
